note_text: Patient seen in clinic for follow-up of lumbar radiculopathy. Findings: straight leg raise positive on the right at 40 degrees; motor strength 4/5 in right ankle dorsiflexion; deep tendon reflex diminished at the right Achilles; sensation to light touch reduced in the L5 distribution. Plan of care discussed; MRI requested.

steps.title: Create the case
steps.say: A coordinator opens an authorization request for an MRI of the lumbar spine with contrast. The platform finds the patient's active coverage and the payer policy in force today.

steps.title: Resolve the policy, with citations
steps.say: The rules engine reads the payer's criteria and checks each one against the chart. Every requirement shows the policy passage it comes from.

steps.title: One missing note, one qualifying lab
steps.say: A search of the policy library in the reviewer's own words, then the two findings that matter: the kidney-function lab qualifies; the neurological examination on file is too old.

steps.title: Attach evidence and submit
steps.say: The clinician's new examination note arrives as a FHIR document. Evidence matching is re-run, a person accepts the links, and the case goes to the payer.

steps.title: The payer denies it
steps.say: The payer's letter says therapy was not shown. The letter carries no reason code, so the classifier reads it, and retrieval finds which criterion the reviewer means.

body.denial_text: After review, the requested service does not meet our medical necessity criteria because a course of physiotherapy of adequate length was not shown.

steps.title: Grounded appeal, physician sign-off, overturned
steps.say: A worker drafts the appeal: every claim cites a policy passage or a chart record. The coordinator cannot sign it; a physician does. The payer reverses, and the metrics update.

body.attestation: Trying to approve as a coordinator.
I reviewed the record and the cited evidence; the appeal is accurate.
